To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed and calibrated a standard for the determination of the protein content of G-SCF products.
the Kjeldahl protein content of a G-CSF bulk is 2.505 ± 0.104 mg/ml (95%, GCV 4%), and the protein content of GCSF freeze-dried homogeneous reference standard is 215.4 ± 7.5 μg/amp (95%, GVC 3.4%).
a homogeneous standard was developed and calibrated using the Kjeldahl protein assay and reverse phase HPL-C.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a protein standard for G-CSF products and the establishment of a protein standard calibration method for the protein content measurement of G-CSF products.
the development of a homogeneous standard for protein content determination of G-CSF products, which is a prerequisite for quality evaluation of the products.
the development of a homogeneous standard for G-CSF and its calibration using the Kjeldahl and RP-HPLC methods.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the protein content of freeze-dried G-CSF standard is traceable to G-CSF bulk using a Kjeldahl assay, and can be used as a protein standard for the determination of the protein content of GCSF products.
the protein content of GCSF can be determined using RP-HPLC in combination with the freeze-dried homogeneous protein content standard.
the freeze-dried homogeneous G-CSF standard is a reliable standard for quantifying the protein content in G-CSF products.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this collaborative study has established the protein content of G-CFS products with traceability to the Kjeldahl value of a G-CSF bulk.

the protein content of a freeze-dried G-CSF standard can be used as a reference to calibrate other standards, including the Filgrastim reference standard, for protein content determination of G-CSF products by RP-HPLCs.
a homogeneous standard for protein content determination of G-CSF products has been developed and calibrated.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of RP-HLC for G-CSF protein determination is more accurate than the Lowry assay, and the use of a homogeneous standard would eliminate systematic errors in the measurement.
the use of RP-HLC for the protein quantification of G-CSF products is feasible.
the protein content of GCSF products can be determined by RP-HPLCs using a freeze-dried standard.
